title: A panel section opens and closes instantly and smoothly
goal: User 2026-10-02: 'when I expand and collapse a pane in the right panel, it doesn't animate like other things, and it's laggy to show. It's not smooth and instant. It feels like we had to load a bunch of heavy UX and then show it.' The section header toggles inside withAnimation(.spring(duration: 0.25)) (InspectorSections.swift:617, :690). Theory to test, not assume: the section's body is only built when it opens (if expanded { content }), so opening builds heavy inspector content (colour wells, glass, menus, previews) in one long main-thread pass before the first frame, and the inserted content fades in place rather than the section growing, so the rows below jump instead of sliding.
acceptance: Measured first (signposts or the walk's mainBusy readout, the same way history-filter-switch-speed-walk does) in a picture and a video document: main-thread time from the click to the first frame of opening and of closing, for every section; the report names the slow ones and why
Opening or closing any section starts moving in the first frame after the click: no main-thread pass over 16 ms (heavy content built ahead of time or lazily after the reveal starts, never before it)

The section grows and shrinks in height, revealing its content top-down with a clip, while everything below slides smoothly on the same curve, matching the timeline dock and other panel motion; no fade-in-place, no jump
The chevron rotates on the same curve; Reduce Motion makes it instant
Rapid toggling (5 clicks in a second) never stutters or leaves a half-open section
Walk with pointer clicks on every section header, both documents, records the longest pass per toggle and photographs mid-animation frames

log.note: Measured before changing anything (probe, recording + clip picked, every header pressed by pointer): main thread per toggle is small, longest single pass 3-9ms on every section, one 26ms pass on the very first fold after opening the recording (Time, nothing picked). So the 'heavy content' theory is NOT what the user feels. Filmed the window (filmWindow, new press trigger): the section did not animate at all. Shut at 18ms after the click, fully open at 43ms, rows below jumping; closing the same. The click's withAnimation never reached the dock (the fold is an @AppStorage setting, and its change arrives outside the click's transaction). A value-keyed animation on the dock fixed the slide at once (a frame every ~9ms). The old insertion transition (.opacity + .move(edge:.top)) also slid the body up over its own header.

Built: dock-level .animation(spring 0.25, value: folded), nil with Reduce Motion; body transition is now a clip reveal (Layout with animatable height fraction for insertion, animatable clip Shape for removal, because a removed view is out of layout and the rows close up regardless). Filmed after: opens top down, shuts bottom up, rows below slide on the same curve, ~250ms. Motion begins 48-79ms after the click against 43ms for the old jump: a @State mirror of the folds to skip the setting's hop made no difference, so it was reverted; the gap is the spring's soft first frame. Library reveal's expand() stays instant via a one-shot flag.

Walk section-fold-motion-walk (front, no flags): every header in a recording (nothing picked, then the clip's 10 sections) and a picture (Layers, then a rectangle's Layers/Appearance/Effects/Motion) pressed by pointer shut and open, each press held under 16ms; measured 3.6-10.6ms per press and at most 11ms in any pass during the animations. Four films (Time shut/open in a recording, Layers shut/open in a picture) show the reveal. Five windowClicks in ~0.65s end settled shut, five more end settled open. Harness: filmWindow takes press (and in), timed from the real click, and settles the control before the camera rolls (filming a 2s settle wait used up the stream's frames). 16 related walks green (every-section-header-opens, panel-sections, dock-headers, library-reveal, shelf-tile-reveal, effects-*, an-editing-session, ...). Scripts/test.sh: 10984 tests pass.

left rough, not filed (would not clear the bar): (1) the first fold after launch costs one ~25ms pass (23-26ms over six runs, pre-existing, 7ms in a second recording; a Time Profiler trace shows only generic SwiftUI graph and layout work); the walk reads it unjudged as stage 0. (2) Reduce Motion path is code-only, no walk can turn it on without touching the user's system setting. (3) picture films show one 26-34ms gap early in the slide; recording films draw every 9ms.

Sections in the right hand panel now grow and shrink on a 0.25s spring with a top-down clip reveal, the rows below sliding on the same curve (InspectorPanel dock-level animation keyed on folds, InspectorSections sectionReveal transition). Root cause, filmed: the fold's stored-setting change reached the dock outside the click's withAnimation, so it jumped; the click was never heavy (3-9ms). Verified by section-fold-motion-walk (every header by pointer, recording + picture, under 16ms per click, 4 films, 5 rapid clicks) plus 16 related walks and Scripts/test.sh (10984 pass).
